top_jobs.job: When a month of new buyers came in on paid ads and 90 days later most never came back, help me find why and fix what they get in the first weeks, so I stop paying full price for every sale
top_jobs.metric: second order rate within 90 days, by month of first order

top_jobs.job: When the inbox fills up and replies and follow-ups slip, help me answer faster, keep every promise and remove the questions at the source, so no customer waits and I stop paying to answer the same question
top_jobs.metric: tickets per 100 orders, and median time to resolution

top_jobs.job: When returns, defects or bad reviews start to rise on a product, help me catch the cause early and send it to the person who can fix it, so the next 500 orders ship right
top_jobs.metric: return rate by product and reason, 60 day

top_jobs.job: When I want to keep my best customers and stop paying ads to reach people who already buy, help me see who makes money and treat them quietly well, so they stay without learning to wait for a sale
top_jobs.metric: repeat rate and gross profit of the top 2 percent of customers, 365 day

jobs.job: Build the cohort grid: second order rate at 30, 60 and 90 days by month of first order, split by first product, channel and first discount, and name the 2 cohorts that fell most
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then the first Monday of each month

inputs.need: 24 months of orders with customer ids, refunds and discount codes
order source for each first order, from link tags
product cost per SKU
what happened each month: sales, stockouts, new ads

steps: Pull 24 months of orders and tie each to one customer by email or phone
Mark each customer's first order month, first product, first channel and first discount code
Count who ordered again by day 30, 60 and 90 in each cohort, from totals
Split each cohort by first product, channel and discount, and hide cells under 50 customers
Name the 2 cohorts that fell most against the 6 month average, and the split that explains it
Check with the founder what changed that month: a sale, a new ad, a stockout
jobs.output: a cohort grid (first order month by day 30, 60 and 90) with splits, plus 2 lines on the cohorts that fell and why
jobs.next: feeds 15-02 (why they hire and leave), 15-04 (reorder reminders) and 21-13 (payback by cohort)

watch.metric: second order rate within 90 days, by month of first order

jobs.drives: repeat revenue per customer, and blended cost per order

jobs.job: Find why customers hire the product and why one-time buyers never order again, from 200 reviews, 200 tickets and a 1 question survey on the thank you page
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then each quarter

inputs.need: reviews with star rating and product
tickets from one-time buyers and from repeat buyers
a thank you page question: what made you buy today
list of one-time and repeat customers
voice of customer quotes already filed

steps: Pull 200 reviews and 200 tickets, half from repeat buyers and half from one-time buyers
Tag each by the moment that made them buy, the result they wanted, what they used before and what nearly stopped them
Add the 1 question survey on the thank you page and read the first 100 answers
Compare repeat buyers with one-time buyers: which moments and doubts differ
Write the top 3 hiring moments and the top 3 reasons for no second order, with 2 quotes each
Founder reads it and marks what rings true and what is wrong
jobs.output: a 1 page jobs map: 3 hiring moments, 3 reasons there is no second order, quotes, and what each suggests we change

watch.metric: second order rate of the cohort after the fix ships

jobs.drives: repeat rate, and new angles for ads

jobs.job: Write the first 14 days after delivery: take the top 10 how-to questions new buyers ask (use, wash, size, fit) and answer them in the delivery email, a day 5 email and a card in the box
jobs.trigger: once, then when a new question enters the top 10

inputs.need: tickets sent within 14 days of delivery
product care, use and size rules
email tool with shipping and delivery flows
a small print run of insert cards

steps: Pull tickets sent within 14 days of delivery and tag each by question
Rank the top 10 questions by count per 100 orders
Write one short answer per question, with a photo or a 20 second clip
Put answers 1 to 3 in the delivery email, 4 to 6 in a day 5 email, and the rest on the insert card and the help page
Founder checks every answer against the product and the claims shelf
Compare how-to tickets and returns for 30 days before and after
jobs.output: 2 live emails, 1 insert card and a help page, each answering named questions
jobs.next: feeds 15-06 (fills blank cells in the matrix) and 14-email-messaging

watch.metric: how-to tickets in the first 14 days after delivery, per 100 orders

jobs.drives: returns from unsure buyers, and second order rate

jobs.job: Find the reorder window for each top product and send a reminder 5 days before it runs out, with no discount on the first touch, tested against a 20 percent holdout
jobs.trigger: once per product, then read each month

inputs.need: orders with repeat purchases per product
email or SMS tool
brand voice and banned words
discount rules

steps: For each of the top 10 products, compute the median days from first to second order
Set the reminder at that median minus 5 days, and a second touch at plus 10 days
Write the reminder in brand voice: what they bought, when it usually runs out, one tap to reorder
Hold out 20 percent of customers who get nothing
After 60 days compare reorder rate and margin with the holdout, and log it as a win or a fail
jobs.output: live reorder flows per product, with a 60 day readout against a holdout

watch.metric: reorder rate within 60 days, flow versus holdout
watch.source: Shopify orders and the email tool

jobs.drives: repeat revenue

jobs.job: Ask customers who went quiet where they went: send a 2 question exit survey to anyone past 2 times their reorder window, and count the reasons and the rivals they name
jobs.trigger: first Monday of each month

inputs.need: lapsed customers past 2 times their product's reorder window
a short survey form sent by email
inputs.from: email tool or a free form

inputs.need: tickets and reviews that name a rival or say they stopped
competitor names and brands to match

steps: List customers past 2 times their product's reorder window with no order
Send 2 questions: did you stop or switch, and if you switched, to what and why
Add tickets and reviews that name a rival or say they stopped
Tag every answer with one reason and the rival named, and check 20 tags by hand
Report the top 3 reasons and the top 2 rivals with counts and 3 quotes, and send product reasons to the product owner
jobs.output: a monthly list: reasons for leaving by count, rivals named, 3 quotes
jobs.next: feeds 03-competitors and 15-14 (causes sent to an owner)

watch.metric: lapsed customers with a stated reason, by reason and rival

jobs.drives: win-back rate and repeat rate

jobs.job: Build the question coverage matrix: every question from tickets, chat, Amazon questions, reviews and site search in rows, every place it could be answered in columns, then fill the 10 biggest blank cells
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then every 2 weeks

inputs.need: 6 months of tickets and chat
Amazon customer questions and buyer messages
inputs.from: Amazon Seller Central, when they sell there

inputs.need: site search terms
reviews that ask or answer a question
product page, FAQ and email text
claims we may make

steps: Pull every question and merge the ones that mean the same thing
Count each question per 100 orders and mark the product it is about
Check each place (product page, FAQ, shipping email, ad, Amazon listing, help centre) and mark answered, half answered or blank
Rank blank cells by count and by how close the question is to buying: size, fit, delivery and returns first
Write the answer for the top 10 blanks, and a person checks each against the claims shelf
Publish the answers and log the date, so the next run shows tickets before and after
jobs.output: a matrix of questions by places, with the top 10 blanks filled and dated

watch.metric: tickets on the 10 filled questions, per 100 orders

jobs.drives: tickets per 100 orders, and product page conversion

jobs.job: Put a clock on every ticket: first reply time, time to resolution, follow-ups owed and reopens, with the order value at stake, and list every breach each morning
jobs.trigger: every morning at 9

inputs.need: tickets with every status change, tag and agent
orders and lifetime spend per customer
reply and resolution targets per ticket type
team hours and who covers weekends

steps: Pull every ticket opened or still open in the last 30 days, with each status change
Compute first reply time and time to resolution in business hours, per ticket and per agent
Mark tickets over target, tickets waiting on us, and follow-ups promised but not sent
Add the customer's lifetime spend and any open order value to each late ticket
Send one morning list: breaches first, sorted by value at stake, each with an owner
jobs.output: a daily breach list, and a 30 day table of median first reply and resolution time by reason and agent

watch.metric: median time to resolution in hours

jobs.drives: repeat rate of customers who had a ticket, and bad reviews

jobs.job: Give every promise made in a ticket a dated follow-up: when an agent writes we will reship, refund or check, create a task, check it happened, and write back to the customer
jobs.trigger: on every ticket closed with a promise, checked each day

inputs.need: closing replies and tags
list of promise phrases and the macros that use them
refunds, reships and tracking numbers
owner for each promise type

steps: Scan closing replies for promise phrases: reship, refund, replace, check with the warehouse, get back to you
Create a follow-up task with a due date and an owner
On the due date check the order: was the refund paid, did the reship get a tracking number
Send the customer a short note: done, with proof, or a new date and why
Report each week: promises made, kept on time, late, and the reopen rate for each
jobs.output: a follow-up list with every promise, its owner, its due date and whether it was kept

watch.metric: reopen rate of tickets closed with a promise

jobs.drives: repeat rate of customers who had a problem

jobs.job: Tag the last 90 days of tickets with one reason from a fixed list of 15, find the reason growing fastest, and put a dollar cost on each reason
jobs.trigger: once, then every Monday

inputs.need: tickets with text and handle time
refunds, reships and store credit
support cost per hour
reason list with 3 examples each

steps: Draft the 15 reasons from 300 sample tickets and write 3 examples for each
Tag every ticket, then check 40 tags by hand and fix the list where it is wrong
Count each reason per 100 orders this week against the last 8 weeks
Cost each reason: agent minutes times cost per minute, plus refunds, reships and credits
Write the top 3 by cost and the 1 growing fastest, each with an owner who can fix the cause
jobs.output: a reason table with count per 100 orders, trend and cost, plus 3 named fixes

watch.metric: share of tickets by top 5 reasons

jobs.drives: support cost per order

jobs.job: Send delivery updates before customers ask: each morning find orders past their dispatch date or stuck in transit for 3 days, and send a 2 line note with a new date
jobs.trigger: every morning

inputs.need: fulfilment status per order
carrier tracking scans
promised dispatch and delivery days per region
email or SMS tool to send the note
order status tickets

steps: List open orders past the promised dispatch date, and shipped orders with no scan for 3 days
Group them by cause: not packed, carrier delay, address problem
Send each customer a 2 line note with the cause in plain words and a new date
Send address problems to a person to call or text the same day
Compare order status tickets per 100 orders for 4 weeks before and after
jobs.output: a daily list of late orders, and a note sent for each

watch.metric: order status tickets per 100 orders

jobs.drives: support cost per order, and bad reviews

jobs.job: Write the support rulebook for a new hire or an AI agent: tone, what each may refund or reship alone and up to what amount, when to hand to a person, and 20 replies for the top reasons
jobs.trigger: once, then when a rule is broken or a new person starts

inputs.need: dollar caps for refund, reship, discount and credit
tone and banned words
current macros, policies and escalation rules
top reasons with example tickets
AI agent action log, if one is used

steps: Ask the founder for limits: refund, reship, discount and credit, each with a dollar cap
Write 20 replies for the top reasons in brand voice, each with the facts to check first
Write the hand-over rules: angry customer, chargeback threat, press or creator, VIP, anything over the cap
A person loads the rules into the helpdesk and the AI agent settings
Each week read 20 closed tickets (AI and human), mark any action over a cap, and fix the rule
jobs.output: a 2 page rulebook, 20 replies in the helpdesk, and a weekly check of 20 tickets

watch.metric: share of tickets answered by someone other than the founder

jobs.drives: founder hours on support, and AI agent mistakes

jobs.job: Build the return table for each product and size: return rate and top reason over 60 days, the full cost of each return, and a flag on any product at 1.5 times its 6 month rate
jobs.trigger: every Monday

inputs.need: returns and refunds with reason codes and notes
inputs.from: Shopify returns, or the returns app

inputs.need: full cost of a return: postage both ways, restock, write-off
product cost per SKU
size chart and product page text

steps: Pull 60 days of returns and join each to product, size, colour and order date
Clean the reason codes into the fixed list and read 20 free text notes by hand
Compute return rate per product and size from totals, and the full cost of each return
Flag products at 1.5 times their 6 month rate, and name the size or reason behind it
Write 1 fix per flag: a size chart line, a photo, a product note, or a supplier call
jobs.output: a return table by product and size with cost, flags and 1 fix each

watch.metric: return rate by product and return reason

jobs.drives: gross profit per order

jobs.job: Catch a bad batch in days: count tickets, reviews and returns that name the same defect per product and purchase order, alert at 5 in 7 days, and list the unshipped orders from that batch
jobs.trigger: every day

inputs.need: tickets with customer photos
new reviews
returns with reasons
purchase order and date received for each batch
stock by batch or date received

steps: Tag each defect mention with product, defect type and delivery date
Map the delivery date to the batch received just before it
Alert when 5 mentions of the same defect hit one batch within 7 days
List orders not yet shipped from that batch and hold them for a person to check
Send the supplier the count, photos and order numbers, and log the claim
jobs.output: a defect alert with batch, count, photos and a hold list

watch.metric: tickets and reviews with the same defect, per batch
watch.source: helpdesk tags, reviews app and purchase order records

jobs.drives: refunds and bad reviews

jobs.job: Answer every 1 and 2 star review within 5 days with a fix, and send each cause to the person who can change the product or the page, tracking how many weeks it stays open
jobs.trigger: daily for replies, every Monday for open causes

inputs.need: new reviews with rating
the reviewer's orders and tickets
reply tone
owner for each cause type

steps: Pull new 1 and 2 star reviews each day with the reviewer's order and tickets
Draft a reply that names the problem and the fix, and a person approves it
Contact the customer privately to make it right, and log what was done
Tag the cause and put it on the work board with an owner and a due date
Each Monday list causes open for over 2 weeks and how many reviews each caused
jobs.output: replies posted within 5 days, and a list of causes with owner and weeks open

watch.metric: share of 1 and 2 star reviews answered within 5 days

jobs.drives: star rating on best sellers, and conversion

jobs.job: Mine 300 reviews of the top 3 rivals on Amazon and their own sites: list what buyers love, hate and wish for, mark the complaints we already solve, and hand 5 lines to copy and 3 notes to product
jobs.trigger: once at onboarding, then each quarter

inputs.need: the 3 rivals with product links
rival reviews from Amazon and their sites
inputs.from: a review export tool, or a person copies them by hand

inputs.need: our own reviews
proof we hold for each claim

steps: Pull 100 reviews per rival, weighted to 1 to 3 stars
Group them into love, hate and wish themes and count each
Mark each hate theme: we solve it, we have the same problem, or unknown
Write 5 lines for ads and pages from the themes we solve, each with our proof
Send the 3 themes we share with rivals to the product owner
Founder checks every claim before it goes to copy
jobs.output: a theme table for 3 rivals, 5 approved lines and 3 product notes

watch.metric: cost per new customer on ads that use the new lines

jobs.drives: conversion on paid traffic

jobs.job: Compare each product's site rating with its Amazon rating, and list what Amazon reviewers complain about that site reviewers do not
jobs.trigger: first Monday of each month, for sellers on Amazon

inputs.need: site reviews and ratings
Amazon reviews on our listings
Amazon return reasons

steps: Pull ratings and reviews per product from both places
For each product with a gap of 0.3 stars or more, group the Amazon complaints
Split complaints into product, listing (wrong expectation), delivery, and fake or reseller units
Write the fix per group: listing copy, image, size note, or a seller report
Recheck the gap 60 days later
jobs.output: a gap table with the Amazon-only complaints and a fix per product
jobs.next: feeds 20-20 (fix the rating) and 20-15 (Amazon question matrix)

watch.metric: star rating per product on site and on Amazon
watch.source: reviews app and Amazon Seller Central

jobs.drives: Amazon buy rate

jobs.job: Rank customers by gross profit over 365 days after returns, shipping and discounts, take the top 2 percent, and drop heavy returners and buyers who only order with a code
jobs.trigger: once, then each quarter

inputs.need: orders, refunds and discounts per customer
product and shipping cost
tickets and reviews per customer

steps: Compute gross profit per customer for 365 days from orders, refunds, shipping and discounts
Rank and take the top 2 percent, with order count, first product and last order date
Drop customers with 3 or more returns, or with a code on every order
Add notes from tickets and reviews: what they bought and what they said
Founder reads the list and removes anyone who should not be on it
jobs.output: a VIP list of about 2 percent of customers, with profit, history and notes

watch.metric: repeat rate and gross profit of the top 2 percent

jobs.drives: profit from repeat customers

jobs.job: Mail a personal letter to the top 50 customers with quiet early access to the next launch through a private link, never announced, and compare what they do in 60 days with 50 similar customers who got nothing
jobs.trigger: before each launch, at most once a quarter

inputs.need: the VIP list
the founder's voice and signature
next launch date and units set aside
letter printing or a handwriting service, and postage
a hidden product page or a code that only works for these 50

steps: Pick 50 VIPs, and hold out 50 with the same profit and recency who get nothing
Write the letter in the founder's voice, with 1 line from each customer's own history
A person reads every letter before it is printed
Set up the hidden page or code with access 7 days before the public launch
Mail the letters, and log who got what and when
At 60 days compare orders, spend and referrals with the holdout, and log it as a win or a fail
jobs.output: 50 letters sent, a private access page, and a 60 day readout against the holdout
jobs.next: feeds 25-experiments (win or fail note) and 15-17 (next quarter's list)

watch.metric: orders and spend from letter recipients versus the holdout

jobs.drives: repeat rate of top customers, and referrals

jobs.job: Count how many Meta purchases come from people who already bought from us, per campaign, work out the cost per truly new customer, and give the ads team a list of campaigns that should exclude past buyers
jobs.trigger: every Monday

inputs.need: campaigns with spend and purchases
orders with link tags and customer history
which campaigns are prospecting and which retargeting

steps: Match orders with a Meta link tag to the customer's order history
For each campaign, split purchases into first orders and repeat orders
Compute cost per new customer as spend divided by first orders, from totals
List prospecting campaigns where over 25 percent of buyers were past customers
Send the list to the person who runs ads to add a past buyer exclusion; ecomOS does not change the account
jobs.output: a campaign table with new and repeat share and cost per new customer, plus an exclusion list

watch.metric: share of Meta purchases from existing customers

jobs.drives: cost per new customer

jobs.job: List customers with 3 or more returns in 180 days, show their share of all refunds, and draft a fair rule for the founder to sign, such as exchange only after the third return
jobs.trigger: each quarter

inputs.need: returns and refunds per customer
full cost of a return
current return policy

steps: Count returns and refund value per customer for 180 days
Compute the share of all refunds from customers with 3 or more returns, and their reasons
Separate fit and defect returns from wear and return
Draft 2 rule options with the money each saves and the sales each could cost
Founder picks one, and it goes into the returns app and the support rulebook
jobs.output: a list of serial returners, their share of refunds, and a signed rule

watch.metric: share of refund value from customers with 3 or more returns

jobs.drives: refunds per order

new_enablers.name: Cohort and repeat view
new_enablers.what: Groups customers by the month of their first order and tracks second order rate, orders, returns and gross profit per customer at 30, 60, 90, 180 and 365 days. Splits by first product, channel, market and first discount, and gives each product its reorder window.
inputs: orders with customer ids for 24 months
powers: which cohorts stopped coming back and when
which first product makes repeat buyers
profit per customer by channel, for bid caps

new_enablers.name: Reason tagger
new_enablers.what: Gives every ticket, return, review and exit survey answer one reason from a fixed list of about 15, plus product, variant and batch. A person checks 20 to 40 tags a week. Counts each reason per 100 orders and puts a dollar cost on it.
inputs: a reason list with 3 examples each
powers: the reason growing fastest this week
what to fix in product, page or delivery
